# bugs #2877: Warning 158 for constant sums that fit in the unsigned char parameter they are passed for

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2877/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17228
- Recommended action: Confirm the decision of bug #3986, apply its patch after the patch for local 0013, and close.
- Patch: [bugs-3986.patch](../../patches/bugs-3986.patch), commit [`f955bae8b`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/f955bae8b9ad37f7d01b4a986ef980754f154ce4). Apply after `local-0013.patch`.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17228 for mcs51, the attached `silly.c` gets warning 158, "overflow in implicit constant
conversion", for the arguments `0xC0 + 41` and `192 + 41` of a function with an unsigned char
parameter. Their value 233 fits, and the call with the argument `233` compiles without the
warning. Each of the three calls passes 0xe9. The file was compiled in the small, medium, large,
and huge models, and with `--stack-auto` in the small and large models, and it gets the two
warnings each time.

The file defines the macros `X` and `Y` and does not use them. As arguments for an unsigned char
parameter they get the warning too, and so does the assignment of `192 + 41` to an unsigned char.

## Cause

The entry for bug #3986 describes the cause. For an unsigned char parameter, `decorateType` in
`src/SDCCast.c` casts the literal operands of `+` to char before `valPlus` computes the constant,
and an int literal becomes a signed char. `192 + 41` becomes -23, and `checkTypes` in
`src/SDCCicode.c` reports that value for the unsigned char. In the fifth comment of bug #2733 a
maintainer calls this ticket similar and names the propagation of `RESULT_TYPE_CHAR` as the cause
there.

## Fix

The patch for bug #3986 fixes this ticket, and another change is not needed. `decorateType`
applies the integer promotions to two literal operands of `+` when the result type is char, and
the sum is computed in int.

## Decision

The patch also adds warning 158 to constant sums, differences, and left shifts whose value does
not fit, such as `u = 200 + 100` for an unsigned char `u`. The entry for bug #3986 has the choices
that a maintainer should confirm.

## Verification

`silly.c` and a file with the statements of the second paragraph of Finding were compiled for
mcs51 by r17228 and by r17228 with the patches of this report, in the six combinations of model
and `--stack-auto` under Finding. With the patches the compiler does not print a message for
them, and its assembly is equal to the assembly of r17228. r17228 with the patch for bug #3986
and without the other patches was not built, and other ports were not tested.

`support/valdiag/tests/bug-3986.c`, the test of the patch, has the call `g (30 * 8 - 1)` for an
unsigned char parameter and the assignments `u = 127 + 1` and `u = 200 + 55`. It does not have
the sums of this ticket.

## Related

- Bugs #2733 and #3094 report this cause.
- The ticket reports that SDCC 3.6 compiles the file without the warning. That was not checked.
